To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
art prices are influenced by stock prices and investor sentiment, and that the relationship between art and stock prices is not constant over time.

(i) there is a significant wealth effect between art prices and equity markets, (ii) gold prices are not significant in the art market, (iii) investor sentiment is a significant driver of art prices, (iv) art prices are more volatile than equity prices and (v) art prices are not cointegrated with stock prices or investor sentiment
the art market behaves as a luxury good, with prices increasing with stock prices, but with the effect being stronger in some market conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the dynamics of art prices and their dependence on the stock market and investor sentiment.
understanding the relationship between the art market and other markets and the nature of the art market as a luxury good.
how the art market is affected by the financial market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
art prices are a luxury good, but the degree of luxury is not constant.
art is a luxury commodity, but that its luxury status varies with the economic environment.
art is a luxury commodity, but the luxury effect is dependent on market conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the art market is a luxury market, but that the wealth effect is not constant.
there is a dynamic wealth effect between art prices and stock prices and the effect is more pronounced in bull markets.
there is evidence of a wealth effect in the British art market and that art can be considered as a luxury good in certain market conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the art market is a dynamic luxury good.
art prices are not independent of equity and gold prices, but that the relationship between them is dynamic, not static.
art prices do not follow a random walk, but rather are a luxury good that responds to wealth effects in a dynamic manner.
